text:
maria: heads up — i'm planning a terraform change to rotate the imagePullSecret for billing-service in the billing-app ns. the change also adds an IRSA role annotation to the service account so the app can access S3. quick review? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345

alex: quick q — are you switching to a projected service-account token for ECR creds, or are we still using a dockerconfigjson secret? i thought kubelet/node IAM handled ECR in most clusters.

maria: we still use a `dockerconfigjson` secret named `ecr-pull-creds`. plan is to rotate that secret via Secrets Manager + lambda. IRSA is only for app S3 access. main worry: terraform change might recreate the SA and accidentally drop imagePullSecrets from pods.

jordan: adding `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation to the SA won't by itself remove imagePullSecrets. imagePullSecrets live on the pod spec. but i have seen terraform modules that force-new on SA metadata, which causes a recreate and then pods get restarted. show the SA + pod yaml?

maria: current SA: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: billing-svc
  namespace: billing-app
  annotations: {}
```
pod spec includes: `imagePullSecrets:\n  - name: ecr-pull-creds`

sam: TLDR — safe to add IRSA annotation, but if you want the AWS SDK in the pod to use web-identity, `automountServiceAccountToken: true` needs to be present on the SA (that's distinct from dockerconfigjson). projected token != dockerconfigjson for image pulls.

alex: also note: the AWS SDKs will use the projected token + role if the role is attached to the SA via the annotation and the cluster OIDC provider is configured. no extra env var required for most SDKs, but verify app side is using the SDK default credential chain.

maria: terraform plan shows the k8s service account resource will be REPLACED (module sets annotations that are force_new). that would delete+recreate -> pods restart. is that acceptable?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: FYI there's an active canary of `billing-v2` in staging, avoid any SA replace during 18:00-20:00 UTC.
jordan: if you want to avoid recreation, add a `lifecycle.ignore_changes` on `metadata[0].annotations` in the k8s SA resource, but then you'll need to apply the annotation some other way. example:```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "sa" {
  metadata {
    name = var.name
    annotations = var.annotations
  }
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations]
  }
}
```
maria: good point. but if we ignore changes, how do we add the IRSA annotation? we could run a one-time `kubectl annotate` in a maintenance window or have a small patch job.
sam: non-destructive approach: during a maintenance window run `kubectl annotate sa billing-svc -n billing-app eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-billing-role --overwrite`. that won't recreate the SA or touch pods.

infra-bot: infra-bot: preflight check complete — cluster has OIDC provider `oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/XXXX`. IAM role trust policy seems to include the OIDC `sub` condition and `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.

maria: ok action plan: 1) hold terraform SA replacement until maintenance window, 2) use `kubectl annotate` patch in the rollout pipeline to set IRSA annotation, 3) keep `imagePullSecrets` as-is and wire up Secrets Manager rotation for `ecr-pull-creds` separately. i'll update the PR to remove the force-new behavior and add a note.
alex: sgtm. ping me on the PR when you update so i can review the plan output.
maria: thanks all — i'll make the changes and schedule the patch during the maintenance window :rocket:
